facts.raw_span: decreased vision in her right eye
Symptoms began 4 days prior to presentation
struck by lightning directly to the right forehead
Uncorrected visual acuity measured 20/50 OD and 20/20 OS
Pupils were symmetric, with no relative afferent pupillary defect
Initial anterior segment examination was normal with absence of cataract
Initial dilated fundus examination showed no apparent abnormalities in either eye
central macular thickening in fundus examination at 2 weeks
mild posterior subcapsular cataract visible in right eye at 7 weeks
Intraretinal cystoid changes and subfoveal ellipsoid zone disruption in the right eye at two weeks post-injury
Restoration of foveal contour with decreased cystoid abnormalities, small subfoveal hyporeflective space, and further loss of outer retinal layers in the nasal macula at seven weeks post-injury
Persistent subfoveal hyporeflective space in the inner retina with interval restoration of subfoveal outer retinal structures at four months post-injury

concepts.why: The patient developed a mild posterior subcapsular cataract in the right eye at 7 weeks after being struck by lightning directly to the right forehead.
The patient presented with central macular thickening and intraretinal cystoid changes in the right eye after being struck by lightning.
The patient experienced decreased vision in the right eye after being struck by lightning, which may be related to traumatic optic neuropathy.
The patient was struck by lightning directly to the right forehead, resulting in various eye injuries, including cataract and macular edema.

It explains the restoration of foveal contour with decreased cystoid abnormalities and further loss of outer retinal layers in the nasal macula at seven weeks post-injury, as well as the persistent subfoveal hyporeflective space in the inner retina with interval restoration of subfoveal outer retinal structures at four months post-injury.

rationales.F03: The patient was directly struck by lightning, which is a strong indicator of lightning-induced injuries.
rationales.F09: The development of a mild posterior subcapsular cataract is a known complication of lightning strikes.
rationales.F08: Central macular thickening is a common finding in macular edema, which can be caused by lightning-induced injury.

frontier_selector.rationale: The patient's symptoms of decreased vision, central macular thickening, and intraretinal cystoid changes are consistent with macular edema, and the history of being struck by lightning supports a lightning-induced cause.
